framework.name: wasp
framework.notes: Not a Next.js app: Wasp (wasp-lang) full-stack framework, 'wasp: { version: "^0.25.0" }' in main.wasp.ts. Client routing is generated by Wasp from route() specs and rendered with React Router 8 (react-router ^8.0.1 in deps), so the app|pages enum does not apply. Spec lives in main.wasp.ts + per-feature *.wasp.ts files. Docs/blog site (template/blog) is a separate Astro 7 + Starlight 0.41 project.

monorepo.notes: No root-level npm workspaces. Four independent projects in one repo: template/app (Wasp app), template/blog (Astro docs/blog), template/e2e-tests (Playwright), opensaas-sh (derived production app stored as diffs). Only template/app/package.json declares workspaces, and those point at Wasp-generated .wasp/out dirs. Root package.json only holds eslint/prettier/tsc tooling.

auth.notes: Wasp's built-in auth (not next-auth/clerk/auth0): authConfig in src/auth/auth.wasp.ts, userEntity "User". Shipped config enables email auth only (email verification + password reset flows). usernameAndPassword, google, gitHub and discord auth methods exist as commented-out config objects with ready getXAuthConfig/getXUserFields helpers in src/auth/userSignupFields.ts, so OAuth is a few uncomments + GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET away but is NOT enabled by default. Admin role = User.isAdmin boolean, granted via ADMIN_EMAILS list or admin UI.

env.notes: Names only; no values recorded. Validation happens at SERVER STARTUP (main.wasp.ts server.envValidationSchema -> src/env.ts zod schema), not at build, so required_at_build is empty. But every field in src/*/env.ts is a bare z.string() with no .optional()/default (except ADMIN_EMAILS which defaults to ''), meaning the server will refuse to boot unless ALL of STRIPE_*, LEMONSQUEEZY_*, POLAR_*, PAYMENTS_*, OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS_S3_*, PLAUSIBLE_* and GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_* are set - even if you only use one payment provider. The repo's own CI proves it: 'we need to set the required env vars even if they aren't actually used by the app ... in order to pass the validation steps'. DATABASE_URL is commented out in .env.server.example because `wasp start db` injects it. Client vars must be prefixed REACT_APP_. The derived opensaas-sh app also uses DOTENV_VAULT* names (Doppler) via .env.vault.

deploy.notes: No Dockerfile, docker-compose or vercel/netlify config anywhere in the repo - Wasp's CLI generates Dockerfiles at `wasp build` time, so docker/standalone_output cannot be read from source. Deployment is two Fly.io apps evidenced by opensaas-sh/app_diff/fly-client.toml (internal_port 8043) and fly-server.toml (internal_port 8080, min_machines_running 1), plus a Fly Postgres DB; Railway is only README-claimed. Command names come from template/app/README.md (start/db) and the Wasp docs flow (build/migrate-dev) - template/app/package.json has NO scripts field at all, so there is no `npm run build`/`npm start`.

tests.notes: 4 Playwright specs (authRedirectTests, demoAppTests, landingPageTests, pricingPageTests) in template/e2e-tests with baseURL localhost:3000 and a webServer that runs the Wasp app itself. vitest 4.1.9 IS a devDependency of template/app but the template ships ZERO unit/component test files. e2e cannot run without real STRIPE_* test keys, an OPENAI_API_KEY and the Stripe CLI listening on /payments-webhook, so it is not a local-only smoke suite.

pitfalls.detail: Server refuses to boot without ~24 secret env vars. Every schema in src/*/env.ts is a bare z.string() with no .optional(), and src/env.ts spreads ALL of them into the app's envValidationSchema, so a fresh clone must set Stripe AND LemonSqueezy AND Polar AND OpenAI AND AWS S3 AND Plausible AND Google Analytics vars just to run `/`. The repo's own CI works around it by copying .env.server.example verbatim.

This is not a normal Node project: template/app/package.json has no scripts field at all, so `npm install && npm run dev` / `npm run build` do not exist. You must install the Wasp CLI globally (`npm i -g @wasp.sh/wasp-cli`) and use `wasp start`, `wasp db migrate-dev`, `wasp build`. Most of node_modules is generated into .wasp/out by the CLI.

Hard Node pin: .nvmrc says 24.14.1 and the CLI/e2e workflows hardcode it; a mismatch with the globally installed Wasp + its generated Prisma client is the classic first failure. Also all four projects carry `min-release-age=7` in .npmrc (supply-chain guard) which will make `npm install <freshly-published-pkg>` fail for a week after release.

App pins next-gen majors across the board (react 19.2.1, typescript 6.0.3, vite ^8.1.0, react-router ^8.0.1, tailwindcss ^4.1.18, vitest ^4.1.9). Adding an ordinary library that expects React 18 / Tailwind v3 / TS 5 will produce peer conflicts; there is no npm overrides block to absorb them.

vitest is declared as a devDependency but the template contains zero unit test files - only Playwright e2e, which itself needs real Stripe test keys, an OpenAI key and `stripe listen` forwarded to /payments-webhook. There is no test you can run offline to prove a change is safe.

Admin routes are declared with only `authRequired: true`, so ANY logged-in user can reach /admin and render its shell; the real gate is `if (!user.isAdmin)` inside src/admin/layout/DefaultLayout.tsx plus per-operation HttpError(403). Copy an admin page without the DefaultLayout wrapper and it leaks data.

Static demo pages ship live: /admin/calendar, /admin/ui/buttons, /admin/settings are UI showcases with no data, and the landing page's example-app carousel + testimonials are other people's products. Budget a cleanup pass so you do not ship "Cool Feature 3".

One shared POST /payments-webhook endpoint dispatches to whichever processor env is configured; misconfiguring the processor/plan IDs gives opaque 500s at checkout time rather than at startup. Payment plan IDs come from env (PAYMENTS_*), never from code.

Repo hygiene trap when vendoring this template: the real app is template/app in a monorepo whose root package.json only has lint/prettier tooling, and opensaas-sh/ + template-test/ are stored as .diff/.copy patch sets applied by tools/dope.sh. Copying the repo root instead of template/ gives a non-app.

verdict.best_for: A founder who will stay on the Wasp framework and wants a free, MIT, batteries-included SaaS base today: verified email auth, Stripe/LemonSqueezy/Polar billing, an admin dashboard with analytics, S3 uploads, a PgBoss cron job and an AI demo, plus a separate Astro docs/blog site.
verdict.weak_for: Anyone who needs mainstream node tooling (no npm run dev/build), a non-Wasp framework, i18n/multi-tenancy/teams, or a test suite that runs offline - none of that is in the code, and the framework choice is the whole app.
verdict.swap_burden: heavy - the repo IS a Wasp spec; queries, actions, routes, auth, jobs and deploy are framework primitives, so leaving Wasp means a full rewrite, while swapping the individual services (payments, email, storage, analytics) is genuinely cheap because they are thin, isolated modules.

opensaas-sh (the live opensaas.sh deployment) was only read as diff/patch files - its real runtime behaviour, Doppler .env.vault contents (recorded by NAME only, never value) and production Fly config were not executed or verified.

Data volumes for the Postgres DB, actual webhook idempotency/security behaviour (see open issues #688/#727/#728), and whether Stripe/Polar/LemonSqueezy sandboxes actually work end-to-end were not testable from source.
